clue.text: Authoritative realist upset by stargazers

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men who followed a star to Bethlehem

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of realist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth realist is dismayed by astronomers' or astrologers' lofty pronouncements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stargazers' reads as astronomers but means the Magi, the wise men who followed the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a magisterial manner is one of commanding, authoritative confidence.

clue.text: Woman not an extreme left-winger?

parts.note: something mild is moderate, the opposite of extreme
a red is a socialist or communist, on the political left

explanation.surface: A question about a woman who is only a moderate socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: See 7 down
Secret ruin unexpectedly found — one must have a good look

definitions.text: one must have a good look

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out other than planned, so the letters of secret ruin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a hidden ruin, which certainly deserves a careful inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer is an official who examines things closely, such as ballot papers, so must look carefully.

clue.text: Trees forming line in German town

indicators.note: in tells us the line letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany

explanation.surface: Trees planted in a row in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad Ems is a German spa town, often just called Ems.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a kind of tree, so the plural names several such trees.

clue.text: Unstable hat being made secure

indicators.note: unstable means wobbly and liable to fall apart, so the letters of hat being are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wobbly hat is being fixed firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something 'in the bag' is as good as won, its success assured or secured.

clue.text: Short woman and attractive girl like boys who show off

indicators.note: short means the word for woman is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A small woman and a pretty girl behaving like boastful lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the last letter of LADY to give LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is the boisterous, swaggering conduct typical of young men showing off.

clue.text: Support one making a dash across Sweden

indicators.note: across means the runner's word stretches over the Sweden letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a bolter is a person or horse that runs off suddenly
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting across Sweden gets backing along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to bolster something is to prop it up or reinforce it.

clue.text: 'Exceptionally great cake' — boastful patisserie may offer it

definitions.text: 'Exceptionally great cake' — boastful patisserie may offer it

parts.words: 'Exceptionally great cake' — boastful patisserie may offer it
parts.note: a cake shop bragging about an extraordinary gâteau suggests the famous chocolate-and-cherry cake from Germany

explanation.surface: A bragging cake shop advertises its wares as exceptionally great.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase hints at the cake's name: a celebrated, rich gâteau a patisserie would proudly promote.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known layered chocolate sponge with cherries and cream, a showpiece cake of patisseries.

clue.text: Fighter — mostly a chum with endless love

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word for chum loses its last letter

parts.note: a mate is a chum or friend

indicators.note: endless means the word for love loses its final letter

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: A boxer, mostly a friend, whose affection runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MATE to MAT, 'endless' trims ADORE to ADOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, a fighter by profession.

clue.text: Spectacular spender lent pots

indicators.note: pots, read as a verb like shoots or knocks about, signals that the letters of spender lent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big spender lends out some spectacular pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pots' looks like the object of 'lent', but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something resplendent is dazzlingly splendid and impressive to behold.

clue.text: Discharges bad emotions dancing in cabarets

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of cabarets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lets off steam by dancing in nightclub shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychology term: to abreact is to release repressed feelings by reliving the experience that caused them.

clue.text: Information provided by one American clever clogs

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
I is the Roman numeral one
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Information supplied by an American know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clever clogs' is British slang for a show-off who is very clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a clever clogs is a brainy person, and a genius is an exceptionally brilliant one.

clue.text: One who loves going to a match?

definitions.text: One who loves going to a match?

parts.words: One who loves going to a match?
parts.note: reads as a sports fan, but a match here is the thing struck to make fire

explanation.surface: A keen sports fan who never misses a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a football game; the person really loves reaching for a match to light fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a person with a compulsion to start fires would love picking up a match.

clue.text: Child with no yen to become captain

indicators.note: with no means the yen letter is taken away

parts.note: kiddy is an informal word for a child
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A child without money grows up to be a captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kidd was a notorious 17th-century Scottish privateer and pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: William Kidd was a famous captain, hanged for piracy in 1701.

clue.text: Artist who has drawn a holy loony

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters of drawn a holy are jumbled

explanation.surface: An artist who has sketched a crazed holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist famed for soup-can and Marilyn prints.

clue.text: A v-very old coin? One can guarantee authenticity

indicators.note: the stammered v-very tells us the coin's name is stammered too, its opening letter doubled

parts.note: a tester was an old English sixpence
a tester was an old English sixpence

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a very old coin is genuine, and an expert can vouch for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'v-very' signals a stammered coin: T-TESTER. A tester was a Tudor shilling, later slang for sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attests is a witness who certifies or confirms that something is genuine.

clue.text: The man taking time in public work? It's too much

indicators.note: in places the man and time letters inside the public work

parts.note: overt means open or public
op is short for opus, a work
he is the man

explanation.surface: A man taking time off within public works, which is just too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something excessive or outrageous is described as going beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Disease and death coming with Eastern rodents mostly

parts.note: the end is death

indicators.note: mostly means the word for rodents loses its last letter

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: Disease and death arrive with rats and mice from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disease' is used loosely as a noun: an endemic is a disease permanently present in a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: an endemic is an illness regularly found among a particular population or place.

clue.text: Warlike god has some good intentions

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even a god of war has some good intentions.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse mythology: the chief god Odin was associated with war, battle and the slain.

clue.text: Plant supposedly poisonous — magistrate has prohibition introduced

indicators.note: introduced means the prohibition is put into the magistrate's title

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A magistrate has brought in a ban on a supposedly toxic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogbane is a plant whose name says it was reputed to poison dogs.

clue.text: Analyse carbon a long way out in space

definitions.text: a long way out in space

parts.note: to parse is to analyse a sentence grammatically
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Analysing carbon found far away in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of astronomical distance, about 3.26 light years, so a long way in space.

clue.text: Circulated edition faded away

parts.note: died means faded away, as a sound dies

explanation.surface: An edition that circulated has now faded from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that swirled round in eddies has circulated, moving in a circular current.

clue.text: Rushed into hospital with fever, delivering tirade

indicators.note: into says the running goes in after the hospital letter

parts.note: ague is a fever with shivering
ran means rushed

explanation.surface: Someone dashed into hospital with a fever, ranting all the while.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a harangue is a long, forceful and scolding speech.

clue.text: Ship from past traversing river

indicators.note: traversing means the word for past lies across the river letter, surrounding it

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A ship from long ago crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth: the Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts.

clue.text: The devil ending in pit in rage

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for rage

parts.note: temper means rage

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of pit

explanation.surface: The devil finishes up in the pit, furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is called the Tempter because he lures people into sin.

clue.text: At home leave chair — almost time for coffee?

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stand is to get up out of a chair

explanation.surface: At home, almost time to get up from the chair and make coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant is quick-dissolving powdered coffee, and the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Thermodynamic sequence in polluting vehicle rather than green one

parts.note: a car burns fuel and pollutes
not as in 'this, not that' means rather than
a bicycle is an environmentally green vehicle

explanation.surface: A thermodynamic process found in a polluting car rather than a green bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics term: the Carnot cycle is the idealised heat-engine cycle of four reversible stages.
